newsitem.title: UK: BZW lost 11.5 mln stg after hedging loss.
newsitem.headline: BZW lost 11.5 mln stg after hedging loss.

text.p: BZW, the investment banking arm of Barclays plc, said it made losses of 11.5 million pounds ($18.6 million) in July 1996, after hedging a trading position which had moved into the red because of "unanticipated and rapid movement in the currency markets."
BZW was responding to newspaper reports and said its management had been fully aware of the position and acted within minutes of the currency fluctuation occurring to reduce the position risk.

BZW said the 11.5 million pounds ($18.6 million) loss was included in its 1996 results which showed a 29 percent fall in pre-tax profits to 204 million pounds. The investment bank added that it had not incurred any material losses within its markets business during 1996.
The case is bound to be compared to NatWest Markets' recent loss of 90 million pounds in interest rate options but analysts said the scale and nature of the loss at BZW was different.
NatWest Markets has admitted to mis-pricing errors that went undetected for two years while BZW claims it took immediate action and was aware of the position before the loss happened.

BZW has been struggling over a major reorganisation of its management which has led to costly changes in personnel and was recently rapped over the knuckles for its actions during the high-profile takeover battle for Northern Electric last year.
